project.name: pictochat-decomp
project.title: PictoChat
project.tagline: byte-matching the DSi's chat app, function by function
project.compiler: mwccarm (CodeWarrior for embedded ARM), a dsi/ build - version NOT yet pinned. Sweep the dsi builds (dsi/1.1, 1.1p1, 1.2, 1.2p1, 1.2p2, 1.3, 1.3p1, 1.6sp1, 1.6sp2); dsi/1.3 is the working guess for a 2009 launch-window system title. Flags (ARM9): -O4,p -enum int -lang c99 -char signed -interworking -thumb -proc arm946e -gccext,on -msgstyle gcc -Iinclude. ARM7: same but -proc arm7tdmi. -thumb is confirmed necessary (mwccarm otherwise emits ARM-mode even for tiny leaf funcs the ROM has as Thumb); override per-function with --flags if a candidate comes out the wrong size.
project.cppNote: If a name starts with _Z (C++ mangled), write C++ with the FIRST LINE exactly //cpp - the build compiles a src file as C++ when its first line is //cpp, else as c99.
project.setup: clone {github} and follow CONTRIBUTING.md. You bring your own dumps (nothing copyrighted is in the repo): your own DSi PictoChat title (assets/pictochat.nds) and your own ARM7 BIOS (assets/bios7.bin). Set up mwccarm (a dsi build) per notes/setup-mwccarm.md, `pip install ndspy capstone pyelftools pyghidra`, then `python tools/extract_pictochat.py` to populate extracted/.
project.readFirst: notes/matching-style.md (matching levers + known walls), notes/tooling.md (the tool suite), and notes/pictochat-layout.md (why the total is Ghidra's estimate, not dsd's). Coordinate your span in CLAIMS.md.
project.submitting: Before opening a PR read CONTRIBUTING.md. Every file you add to src/ MUST byte-reproduce the binary (tools/match.py green) - that is the only merge gate. One matched function per src/arm9/<symbol>.c|.cpp or src/arm7/<symbol>.c|.cpp (first line //cpp for C++). Claim your span in CLAIMS.md first. A logic-correct but NOT byte-exact draft is parked with a `// NONMATCHING:` marker via tools/nonmatching.py - it does not count as matched and must not be presented as a match. Before hand-writing anything, try the free tiers: `python tools/sync_ledger.py --apply` then `python tools/cross_match.py --other-repo ../sm64ds-decomp` (cross-project + template matching has already landed dozens with no hand-writing).
project.rules: only your own legally dumped DSi title and BIOS; never commit the ROM, the BIOS, firmware, or anything extracted/derived from them (see .gitignore) - the repo holds only original work: scripts, hand-written C, notes. Import struct/field knowledge (see CREDITS) but write all C from scratch.
project.nearMissNote: If a function will not fully match after real effort, do not discard your best attempt - keep the closest compiling draft parked as NONMATCHING (tools/nonmatching.py); it is the highest-yield starting point for a later match, and most matches now start from someone's stored draft or a cross-project hit.

matchConventions.srcLayout: src/arm9/<symbol>.c|.cpp and src/arm7/<symbol>.c|.cpp, one matched function each
matchConventions.decompMarker: each src file carries a `// decomp: <module> <addr>` marker (tools/ledger.py MARKER_RE) that ties it to a function address
matchConventions.ledger: tools/ledger.py + tools/sync_ledger.py (marker-based, catches committed src/ up)
matchConventions.nonMatching: tools/nonmatching.py parks logic-correct, not-byte-exact drafts with a `// NONMATCHING:` marker

project.progressNote: Matched function COUNT is computable from committed src/ alone; the TOTAL count and percentage come from Ghidra's function estimate (extracted/, git-ignored, ROM-derived), so a precise percentage needs a local extracted/ - see notes/pictochat-layout.md. dsd's own function search does not finish for this title.

GITHUB_TOKEN.note: Read-only GitHub token. Raises the API rate limit (anonymous is 60/hr) so contributor stats and PR-based match attribution work. A fine-grained token with public-repo read access is enough - stored encrypted on your machine, never shared.

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.note: Only if you drive the model-assisted draft tools (tools/m2c_draft.py, tools/ghidra_draft.py, the permuter loop) over the API instead of from an editor session.
